transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-03
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Ava (Redwood CSM), Luis (Northshore), Priya (Northshore), Samir (Northshore), Eleanor (Northshore)

Summary:
- Kickoff scoping for a POC to characterize traffic shape, QPS/concurrency, and input/output token distribution for Northshore's in-store assistant feature.
- Success criteria: p90/p95 tail latencies under target, predictable cost per 1k requests, and no data leakage; pilot planned for hosted environment then Dedicated if needed.
- Action items and timeline agreed (see action items).

Topics:
- Workload portrait: QPS, concurrency, burst patterns
- Token distributions: user prompt sizes, response sizes, typical system prompts
- Benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, token cost model
- Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2/ISO questions
- Pilot timeline and success gating

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: alright, everybody, thanks for joining, uh sorry for the slight schedule shift. this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. quick intros?
[00:12] Luis: hi, i'm Luis, head of platform at Northshore. we've got Priya, Samir, and Eleanor on the line. thanks for doing this.
[00:18] Priya: hi everyone.
[00:20] Maya: hey, Maya here, i'm the SE who'll run the benchmarks with you. Diego here will help with the harness.
[00:26] Diego: hi all.
[00:28] Eleanor: Eleanor, product — i'll own success criteria on our side.
[00:31] Jordan: great, quick agenda — surface traffic shape, agree success criteria, map out data/benchmarks, and lock next steps. sound good?
[00:38] Luis: yep. our immediate need: we want to validate that the assistant can run at scale in production for holiday season traffic spikes. we expect burst days.
[00:47] Jordan: understood. can you give us some numbers — baseline QPS, peak QPS, expected concurrency?
[00:52] Priya: baseline is about 12 qps globally for the assistant, peak observed during promos is around 220 qps for short windows (2-5 minutes). concurrency on a single region, we see up to 45 concurrent sessions, but those have a lot of short requests — five to 15 tokens in many cases — though some sessions do full receipts or image-to-text which go longer.
[01:15] Samir: and an important nuance — traffic is geo-shifted and bursts can land in one region causing hot-shards. we need to avoid cold starts causing tail latencies.
[01:24] Maya: good -- that's helpful. when you say 12 qps baseline, is that averaged over an hour or over 24h?
[01:30] Priya: that's 24h-average. hourly daytime average is closer to 20 qps.
[01:35] Jordan: for the POC we typically ask for a 7-day capture of traffic to sample QPS and token length distributions. you mentioned many short requests — can you share percentiles? do you have p50/p90 token lengths?
[01:46] Priya: rough numbers: p50 prompt tokens ~14, p90 ~74, p99 ~320. responses p50 ~20, p90 ~160, p99 ~800 — the p99's are heavy because of receipt summarization flows.
[02:02] Diego: we always see that the long-tail heavily impacts KV cache and memory usage for transformer models; it's important for us to model token distribution not just average tokens. (mis-typed as kv cash in some transcripts)
[02:14] Luis: yes and one more: we use system prompts + user prompts; system prompt is about 250 tokens in some of the advanced assistants.
[02:21] Maya: okay, that helps. success criteria — what are you measuring? Eleanor, do you want to go first?
[02:27] Eleanor: sure. product needs: p95 end-to-end latency under 450ms for conversational flows, p99 under 900ms for typical user flows. for long receipts we can tolerate up to 2s but we want to quantify. also cost per 1k requests should be under $x (will give number offline), and no customer data leaves region.
[02:46] Jordan: good — performance and cost gating plus data residency. from Redwood's side we want to propose a two-stage pilot: hosted benchmark run to mirror traffic (2-3 days of scheduled runs) then a Dedicated or private trial for isolation if numbers need improvement.
[02:58] Priya: timeline? holiday season is mid-December so we need results and recommendations by end of November ideally.
[03:05] Jordan: okay that gives us a tight window. our usual plan: 1) receive 7d traffic sample by 2027-11-10, 2) we produce a sizing worksheet + synthetic replay setup by 2027-11-12, 3) run hosted bench week of 2027-11-15, 4) analysis/deltas and recommendations by 2027-11-22.
[03:20] Samir: about security — we will need SOC2 evidence and SAML SSO for the console; if we move to Dedicated we need VPC peering and customer-managed KMS.
[03:30] Ava: we can share SOC2 and ISO docs, and the Dedicated checklist. for VPC we will need contact points and firewall rules; Diego can help walk through the peering.
[03:39] Diego: yes i'll follow up, and we have an onboarding doc for VPC peering.
[03:43] Priya: another point — we do some annotation/inference flows that are bursty with many concurrent small requests (50-100ms real time). how do you model very short latencies?
[03:55] Maya: we instrument tail-latency in the harness. we simulate tiny prompt sizes and very high qps to exercise the mux and batching. we also measure token-level throughput and effective batch sizes; that lets us predict cost and latency trade-offs.
[04:08] Jordan: also worth discussing fallback policies — if the verified model can't meet tail SLOs, do we gracefully degrade to a smaller model or to an async job? is that acceptable for you?
[04:19] Eleanor: yes, degrade to async for heavy receipts is ok, but for interactive chat we need graceful fallback to a smaller model.
[04:26] Priya: we also want to know the unit economics of quantization — if you suggest 4-bit quant, what's the observed quality delta for our prompts?
[04:34] Maya: we'll include quality regression checks using your eval prompt set; we'll measure token-level perplexity-ish proxies and a small eval to make sure reductions don't cause hallucinations.
[04:43] Luis: on cost alignment: can you model cost per 1k responses across model variants and batch sizes? we need a simple chart for execs.
[04:50] Diego: yes — we provide a cost model that maps QPS, tokens per response, and chosen runtime (fp16 vs q4) to $/1k and to GPU utilization.
[05:00] Samir: networking question: in hosted benchmarks, will token streaming emulate our TCP window sizes and client concurrency? we had issues where bench traffic looked different than production because of client-side backpressure.
[05:12] Maya: good call. we'll mirror TCP-level patterns using the replay harness and can ingest your client SDK logs to emulate concurrency and pacing.
[05:20] Priya: about measurement — which latencies do you measure? server-side generation only, or end-to-end including network and client SDK?
[05:27] Jordan: we'll provide both. server-side generation stats (token throughput, p50/p95/p99 generation latencies), plus end-to-end which includes transit time. for SLOs you said p95 450ms end-to-end, so we'll make sure the replay includes a network latency model that matches your regions.
[05:42] Eleanor: what about warm cache behavior? some of our sessions have repeated prefixes, can you model prefix KV cache hit rates?
[05:50] Maya: yes we simulate prefix cache warmup and measure effective cache hit rate. we also produce suggestions for prefix caching TTLs to reduce per-token cost.
[05:58] Luis: one constraint — we cannot share raw PII. the traffic has customer names and receipts. we will sanitize but keep token lengths representative.
[06:06] Jordan: totally expected. the worksheet will list fields to sanitize; hashed ids and token counts are fine.
[06:11] Priya: benchmarks — what are the model candidates for the POC? we are considering an Llama-based open model and possibly a smaller in-house distilled transformer.
[06:21] Maya: we typically test 2-3 variants: a production-sized open model (e.g., 13B q4), a smaller 7B quantized, and sometimes a transformer distilled baseline. we'll also measure a 'fallback micro' for interactive fallback.
[06:35] Samir: how do you handle KV cache memory on GPUs for long context? our receipts hit up to 8k tokens sometimes.
[06:43] Diego: we track KV memory, and the harness will show memory per-request distribution; if we see out-of-memory at 8k we recommend sequence-length truncation or sharded KV strategies.
[06:52] Priya: what about concurrent model instances? do you model multi-tenant on a node?
[06:58] Maya: yes, the runtime can run multiple model instances and we simulate co-located tenants; we produce effective throughput per GPU as a function of concurrency.
[07:06] Jordan: let's talk throughput math briefly — if your peak is 220 qps for 5 minutes, with average response tokens of 160 at tail that's X tokens per second. our sizing worksheet will convert that into GPU-second requirements.
[07:19] Priya: can you show an example of that conversion?
[07:22] Diego: sure -- (diesgo stumbles on a name in transcript) example: 220 qps * 160 tokens = 35,200 tokens/s. if model throughput is 8k tokens/s per GPU at target latency, you'd need 4-5 GPUs to keep tail latency. but effective batching can improve that.
[07:39] Samir: how do you account for latency variance with batching? sometimes big batches increase p99 beyond SLO.
[07:45] Maya: we produce a latency vs batch-size curve and pick batching windows that optimize cost while keeping p99 within bounds. continuous batching helps reduce variance. we also implement dynamic batch caps during bursts to avoid overly large batches.
[07:58] Eleanor: any telemetry we need to expose in our app to better measure SLOs?
[08:03] Jordan: instrument request token counts, client-side queue times, and response byte sizes. we'll provide a telemetry spec.
[08:10] Priya: about evaluation — can you run A/B tests during POC? we'd like to compare model variants on quality metrics as well as latency.
[08:18] Maya: yes; our harness supports side-by-side runs and retains outputs for diff-based eval. we can integrate your human eval set too.
[08:26] Luis: what are the deliverables at the end of the pilot?
[08:29] Jordan: a bench report with latency quantiles (p50/90/95/99), GPU utilization, collision maps for regions, cost projection per 1k requests, recommended runtime config (batching, q-profile), and an ops runbook for rollout.
[08:41] Priya: good. for the runbook we need specific autoscaling thresholds and recommended instance types.
[08:47] Diego: we'll provide autoscaling knobs tied to token/sec and in-flight request counts; also suggested GPU families.
[08:54] Jordan: timeline recap — Jordan to share sizing worksheet by 11/05, Priya to provide data by 11/10, Maya to run hosted bench week of 11/15, deliverable by 11/22. does that work?
[09:06] Eleanor: yes that works.
[09:08] Samir: one more item: SOC2 docs and the Dedicated spec before we sign off on a dedicated path.
[09:14] Ava: i'll attach SOC2/ISO and the Dedicated checklist in the follow-up email.
[09:19] Priya: anything else on the quality gates? we want false positive rates and hallucination checks.
[09:25] Maya: we'll include a small hallucination check and automatic regression alerts tied to your eval set; if quantization causes >3% drop on key metrics we'll flag it.
[09:33] Jordan: ok, let's open the floor for quick Q&A.
[09:36] Luis: curious about data retention during the hosted bench; do you keep logs longer than 30 days?
[09:41] Ava: by default hosted bench logs retained 30 days, but we can arrange shorter retention or ephemeral mode for the bench.
[09:49] Priya: for the synthetic replay, we need the harness to randomize session ids while preserving length distributions — will you do that?
[09:57] Diego: yes — the replay anonymizes ids but keeps token-length seq and pacing.
[10:02] Eleanor: final ask — can you produce an executive one-pager with the cost delta across three model variants?
[10:09] Jordan: yes — we'll include a 1-pager.
[10:12] Jordan: ok, thanks everyone. quick recap of action items?
[10:16] (recap read out)
[10:18] Jordan: Jordan: send sizing worksheet + bench template (due 2027-11-05). Maya: prepare initial harness and runbook (due 2027-11-12). Priya: provide 7-day anonymized traffic sample (due 2027-11-10). Samir: provide security contacts for peering (due 2027-11-09). Ava: send SOC2 and Dedicated checklist (today).
[10:35] Luis: thanks, talk soon.
[10:36] Jordan: thanks all. meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: ocassional mishears (KV cache -> KV cash; Diego's name mis-transcribed once). occasional overlaps.
